insight.title: Coffee Lids Were Redesigned Because of Your Nose
insight.subtitle: The raised dome on your morning cup isn’t there to make room for foam—it’s an ergonomic trick to keep you from walking blindly into traffic.
insight.notificationHook: The real reason coffee lids are domed

sections.text: Ever wonder why take-out coffee lids evolved from flat plastic discs to raised, hollow domes? It wasn’t a styling trend, nor was it designed to make room for fancy foam.
It was an ergonomic fix for your nose. Flat lids forced you to tilt your head backward to sip, blinding your forward vision and causing spills while walking.
The dome creates "nose space." By letting your face fit into the cup, the lid allows you to drink comfortably while keeping your head level and your eyes forward.
It keeps your eyes on the street, not your lap.
